inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, flat. 4,037m Class A + B ordinary shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 release) + ~82m treasury-method dilution from RSUs/options (Q3 diluted 4,392m less basic 4,081m less 229m convertible-note shares) less ~69m shares for the ~$226m repurchased in October 2026 (the $400m Sep+Oct programme less $174m already in Q3 cash flow, at an assumed ~$3.25). The $1.5bn zero-coupon convertible (229.0m shares, conversion price ~$6.55, far out of the money) is carried as DEBT and excluded from the count; the 26m warrants are out of the money. Held flat because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: Equity-settled share-based payments in the cash flow statement / Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation: 9M 2026 $189m + Q4 2025 $45m = $234m TTM. No separate cash tax on net-share settlement is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 throughout).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.5% in USD (the flows' reporting currency): US 10-year ~4.3% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 + ~1.2pp for Southeast Asian country and currency-translation risk (revenue earned in IDR, VND, MYR, THB, PHP, SGD). The balance sheet is net cash, so WACC is effectively cost of equity. The same rate is used in every scenario: regulatory, competitive and credit risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt. Lease liabilities (~$0.27bn) sit inside reported loans and borrowings ($2,070m) and therefore inside net debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from flows. Ongoing lease renewal is charged through the capex line, which follows Grab's own Adjusted FCF definition (capital expenditures including assets acquired under lease arrangements: $152m for 9M 2026 versus $87m of cash PP&E and intangibles).
inputs.nci_treatment: Deducted once, in the bridge, at Q3 2026 book value ($503m, mostly the digital-bank minorities in GXS, GXBank and Superbank). Flows are consolidated at 100%. Put liabilities to NCI (inside 'other liabilities', which rose from $169m to $684m in 2026) overlap the same minority claims and are NOT deducted a second time; see key risks.
inputs.notes: MODEL: scenario-weighted owner-FCF DCF via the Drivers route, with an explicit digital-bank adaptation. Grab straddles two routing rows (consumer-internet marketplace + deposit-taking lender). Financial Services is ~12% of FY2026 revenue (18% in Q3) and roughly break-even at segment Adjusted EBITDA, so a separate residual-income leg would be valuing a start-up bank on ~zero earnings; instead the lending business is kept INSIDE the consolidated flows and its balance sheet is treated as operating capital: (1) flows are built on Grab's Adjusted EBITDA, which is after deposit interest cost and after net impairment losses on loans; (2) customer deposits ($2,703m) are operating funding, not net debt, and the loan book ($2,534m net) is the operating asset that earns the Financial Services revenue, so neither is in the bridge; (3) the equity capital that loan growth absorbs is charged as a NEGATIVE working-capital capture on revenue growth (Grab's Adjusted FCF excludes loan and deposit movements, so nothing else would charge it; 9M 2026 loans disbursed net $814m against $209m of deposit inflow); (4) the part of the liquidity pool that belongs to depositors or is trapped as bank liquidity is removed from net cash in the bridge. FY0 = FY2026E at the guidance midpoint ($4.15-4.20bn revenue, $790-800m Adjusted EBITDA; 9M actual $3,064m / $560m), so Y1 = FY2027. NET CASH: Grab's reported gross cash liquidity $7.1bn at 30 Sep 2026 (cash $2,848m + time deposits and marketable securities, current and non-current) less ~$226m October buybacks and the $60m foodpanda Taiwan break fee payable in Q4 = $6,814m; total debt $2,070m is all loans and borrowings (the $1.5bn convertible, classified current because of the 2028 holder put, bank loans mostly secured on the rental fleet, and leases). INTEREST: finance income is outside Adjusted EBITDA so it is stripped from the flows by construction and the cash that earns it is in the bridge. last_fcf = TTM Adjusted FCF $533m (company definition, 9M 2026 $457m + Q4 2025 $76m) - SBC $234m - interest received $157m = $142m. reported_fcf is Grab's Adjusted FCF, not IFRS OCF less capex, because IFRS operating cash flow (TTM ~$121m) nets loan disbursals and deposit flows and is not a measure of operating cash generation. Adjusted EBITDA also excludes M&A, restructuring and legal/regulatory settlement costs (~$36m in 9M 2026, about 1% of revenue and recurring in practice); the base margin path sits below management's 2028 target partly for that reason. BUYBACKS: $574m repurchased in 9M 2026 plus ~$226m in October, $500m authorisation remaining; the flat share count is being funded in cash (repurchases exceed SBC).

equity_bridge.item: Bank liquidity held against customer deposits (not available to shareholders)
equity_bridge.note: 25% of $2,703m customer deposits at 30 Sep 2026. Floor is the $169m by which deposits exceed the net loan book; 25% allows for regulatory liquidity buffers at GXS, GXBank and Superbank. Judgment, not a disclosed figure.
Q3 2026 statement of financial position; up from $29m after Superbank consolidation and minority subscriptions into the banks

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management 2025-2028 revenue CAGR target (~20%) haircut to 18% for FY2027; equity CAGR is not usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.6% FY2022-FY2025; FY2020 equity was negative before the SPAC recapitalisation) diverges from revenue CAGR (33%) by far more than 30 points. Book value is flat because cumulative losses and buybacks offset SBC issuance, so it carries no growth signal. EPS and owner FCF were negative at the start of both windows (first IFRS profit FY2025; owner FCF was -$1,292m in FY2022 and still -$122m in FY2025), so no CAGR is defined.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF history (Adjusted FCF - SBC - interest received): FY2022 -1,292; FY2023 -721; FY2024 -308; FY2025 -122; TTM Q3 2026 +142. The business crossed owner-FCF breakeven only in 2026. SBC has fallen from 29% of revenue (FY2022) to under 6%.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Grab's Adjusted EBITDA / revenue. FY2026 guidance 19.0%, Q3 2026 21.3%. FY2028 lands at ~$1.37bn on ~$5.7bn revenue against management's $1.5bn target (a ~9% haircut).
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Cash tax paid was $89m in FY2025 and $53m in 9M 2026 against owner EBIT of roughly $80m and $195m: profitable entities (Singapore 17%, Malaysia 24%, Indonesia 22%) pay while loss-making entities give no group shield. 22% is the blended statutory rate of the profit pools; no credit is taken for the accumulated losses.
base.wc_capture_note: Negative: equity capital absorbed by loan-book growth in GrabFin and the digital banks, net of deposit funding and of the marketplace's modest payables float.

scenario_narratives.base: Grab keeps compounding monthly transacting users and order frequency in an under-penetrated region, but lands a little short of its own 2028 plan: revenue grows 18% then 16% (management targets ~20% a year to 2028) and Adjusted EBITDA reaches ~$1.37bn in FY2028 rather than $1.5bn. Deliveries margin keeps rising on advertising, Mobility margin is flat as the Indonesian two-wheel commission cap and driver-supply incentives offset scale, and Financial Services moves from break-even to a modest contributor as the loan book seasons. Margin matures at 29% of revenue, SBC falls to 3%, and loan growth keeps absorbing equity capital equal to a fifth of each year's revenue increase.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2028 targets are beaten: FY2028 Adjusted EBITDA near $1.6bn on ~$6.0bn revenue. Advertising scales toward the share of Deliveries GMV seen at mature peers, the Indonesian cap stays confined to two-wheel rides, a rational duopoly with GoTo (or a combination) lets incentives fall as a share of GMV, and the digital banks plus Stash become a second profit engine funded mostly by deposits rather than Grab's own cash. Margin matures at 33%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulation and competition take the operating leverage. Indonesia extends the commission cap to four-wheel rides and other governments copy it, GoTo, Xanh SM and Shopee keep incentives rising as a share of GMV (10.7% in Q3 2026, up 64bp on the year), and a regional credit cycle hits a $2.7bn loan book that tripled in a year and has never been through one. Growth fades to mid-single digits by FY2030, Adjusted EBITDA margin stalls at 22%, and lending consumes more of Grab's own cash.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): the regulatory risk is not hypothetical, since Indonesia cut the two-wheel commission from 20% to 8% in July 2026, and the loan book is unseasoned. Base 50%: already a haircut to management's 2028 targets. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs three independent things at once, namely contained regulation, competitive rationality in Indonesia and Vietnam, and a clean credit outcome in the banks.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Grab is valued as one consolidated operating business on owner free cash flow: Adjusted EBITDA less share-based compensation, cash tax, capital expenditure including leased assets, and the equity capital its growing loan book absorbs. Roughly a third of the base-case value is the net cash pile, taken after setting aside the convertible notes as debt, bank liquidity owed to depositors and minority interests. The operating business only crossed owner-FCF breakeven in 2026, so most of the remaining value depends on margins that have not yet been earned; the base case assumes Grab falls modestly short of its 2028 targets.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net cash is about a third of base value and is a judgment: $7.1bn of gross liquidity includes depositor-funded assets, and the 25% liquidity set-aside is an estimate. Each further $500m treated as unavailable is worth about $0.12 a share.

Put liabilities to minority shareholders (inside 'other liabilities', up from $169m to $684m during 2026) are not deducted on top of the $503m NCI. If they prove additive rather than overlapping, value is up to ~$0.15 a share lower.

The lending business is modelled inside consolidated flows with a working-capital charge rather than as a separately capitalised bank. If loan growth has to be funded from Grab's own cash faster than assumed (9M 2026: $814m of net disbursals against $209m of deposit inflow), cash conversion is lower than modelled.
Take-rate regulation: an extension of Indonesia's commission cap to four-wheel rides is in the bear case only.
The convertible is treated as $1.5bn of debt. Above ~$6.55 a share it becomes 229m shares instead, which caps upside in the bull case by roughly 5%.
Adjusted EBITDA excludes M&A, restructuring and legal settlement costs that recur at about 1% of revenue.
